chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked him about a man who said:

to his غلام, “I will free you on the condition that I marry you to this bondwoman of mine. Then if you marry in addition to her or take a concubine, one hundred dinars will be due from you.” So he freed him upon that condition, then he married or took a concubine. Is one hundred dinars due from him, and is his condition valid?
He said: “His condition is binding upon him.”

key_terms.أُعْتِقُكَ: I will free you; a declaration of emancipation
key_terms.تَسَرَّيْتَ: you take a concubine; entering into surriyah/concubinage
key_terms.جَارِيَتِي: my bondwoman; the female slave to whom marriage is proposed
key_terms.شَرْطُهُ: his condition; the stipulated contractual term
key_terms.مِائَةُ دِينَارٍ: one hundred dinars; the specified financial liability
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: it is valid or binding in law

ai.seo_question: Is a condition attached to emancipating a slave legally binding in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning emancipation tied to a stipulated condition. It indicates that when a slave is freed upon a specific condition relating to marriage and financial liability, that condition is valid and enforceable against him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3446 - Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah asked him about a man who said to his slave, "I will free you on the condition that I marry you to this bondwoman of mine. However, if you marry another woman or take another concubine, you will be liable for one hundred dinars."

Then he freed him based on this condition, and the slave either married another woman or took another concubine.
Abd al-Rahman asked: "Is he liable for the one hundred dinars, and is his condition valid?"
Imam (as) said: "His condition is valid, and he is liable for it."
